title: PhysxContactReportAPI
summary: Registers a rigid actor (including a standalone static collider), or every link of an articulation, for contact reporting. A standalone static collider reports on CPU simulation and GPU dynamics with CPU readback; on DirectGPU its sensor row remains but reads zero force. On a separate child collider, the API enables sensor selection on CPU simulation and GPU dynamics with CPU readback but does not enable the owning body's reporting. Read by the runtime at actor creation, not by the parse library; without the API in usd-schemas nothing is registered even if the attributes are authored.
producer_scope: The threshold is published at its resolved value (raw fallback 1.0 when unauthored); the reportPairs relationship only when authored, an authored empty target list being an empty row.

columns.name: physxContactReport:threshold
columns.absent: One tolerances length (1 / metersPerUnit): 1 on a meter stage, 100 on a centimeter stage. Ambiguous-fallback collapse: a column that reads exactly 1.0 is treated as unauthored and yields the same units-scaled default, so writing the raw fallback literally is equivalent to omitting the column, and an intended threshold of exactly 1.0 cannot be expressed on a non-meter stage.
columns.notes: No PhysX getter for the runtime's per-actor report threshold (it lives in the runtime's contact report registry, not on the PxActor): no verify block. Live updates of the column are honoured.

columns.name: physxContactReport:reportPairs
columns.absent: Wildcard: contacts with EVERY other actor are reported. This is decided by whether the relationship is present, not by the target count: a relationship that is present but empty registers nothing, and a present relationship whose targets all fail to resolve to live objects also registers nothing rather than widening into the wildcard.
columns.notes: Path-dictionary ids in USD target order. A hand populator that wants report-all must omit the column; writing an empty row silences reporting for the actor.

interactions.rule: Registered once per rigid actor at creation; on an articulation root every link is registered with the same threshold and pairs.

A separate child collider carrying PhysxContactReportAPI is eligible as a contact sensor on CPU simulation and GPU dynamics with CPU readback. Enable reporting on its owning body, owning articulation link, or articulation root as well to avoid depending on reports from the other actor in each contact pair. If neither actor reports matching contacts, the child sensor reads zero. Author threshold and reportPairs on the reporting actor or articulation root, not on the separate child collider. A standalone static collider is its own rigid actor and enables reporting on CPU simulation and GPU dynamics with CPU readback; on DirectGPU its sensor row remains but reads zero force. DirectGPU session queries omit separate child-collider rows; select a dynamic body or articulation link to read forces instead.
The default threshold scales with the tolerances length; the authored value does not.

findings.summary: Because ovstage reports every column as authored, the consumer distinguishes authored from unauthored by comparing against the raw schema fallback 1.0; an authored 1.0 collapses to the units-scaled default (1 / metersPerUnit). Same shape as the character controller contactOffset/stepOffset case.
